pairs.subject: data-retention
pairs.evidence: src/lib/db/retention.ts:1005 The org receives scan counts only after the entire repo prune returns, so a later batch failure loses counts from earlier committed batches.

techniques.evidence: src/features/admin/settings/DataErasureDialog.tsx:39 The UI requires case-sensitive equality although the server treats org slugs case-insensitively; the technique explicitly rejects comparisons stricter than the identifier's equality rule.

src/lib/db/retention.ts:1190 Below-floor policies are correctly refused unless RETENTION_FORCE=1, but the audit payload and run summary do not record whether that bypass was active, as the technique requires.

src/lib/db/retention.ts:1016 Execution ages out existing digests, but the dry-run branch returns before this sweep and leaves digestsDeleted initialized to zero, understating the destructive population.

src/lib/db/retention-policy.ts:136 Nullable persisted org windows inherit centralized defaults through resolveRetention; explicit zero remains unlimited, defaults retain everything, and disabled windows bypass deletion.

src/lib/db/retention.ts:345 Batching and budget checks exist, but committed counts remain local until this successful return; a subsequent selection or transaction failure rejects the helper and discards those counts from the summary.
